title: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Act 1991

sections.shortTitle: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Act 1991
sections.description:
Short title and commencement

ACT II OF 1991
ACT II OF 1991
SINDH INSTITUTE OF UROLOGY AND
TRANSPLANTATION ACT, 1991
1. Short title
and commencement: ‑(1) This Act may be called the Sindh Institute of
Urology and Transplantation Act, 1991.
(2) It shall come into force on and from the 22nd
October, 1990.

sections.shortTitle: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Act 1991
Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Act 1991
sections.description:
Establishment of the institute

ACT II OF 1991
ACT II OF 1991
SINDH INSTITUTE OF UROLOGY AND
TRANSPLANTATION ACT, 1991
3. Establishment of the Institute.‑‑(l) An Institute to be
called the Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation shall be established
by reconstituting and re‑organizing the Urology Department of the Dow
Medical College and Civil Hospital, Karachi.
(2) The Institute shall be a
body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal with power to
acquire, hold and dispose of property, both movable and immovable, and shall by
the name specified in subsection (1) sue and be sued.

sections.shortTitle: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Act 1991
sections.description:
Functions of the institute

ACT II OF 1991
ACT II OF 1991
SINDH INSTITUTE OF UROLOGY AND
TRANSPLANTATION ACT, 1991
4. Functions of the Institute: ‑The functions of (he
Institute shall be as follows:‑‑
(1) to undertake treatment and
acquire latest physical facilities necessary for carrying out investigation of
urological diseases including renal failure necessitating dialysis or
transplantation;
(2) to develop methodology and
standardise techniques for the investigation of various urological diseases:
(3) to undertake teaching in
the principles of surgery with emphasis in urology in the clinical batches of
the Dow Medical College, Karachi;
(4) to undertake post‑graduate teaching
programmes such as M.S., M.D., F.C.P.S., M. Phil. and Ph. D. in urology,
nephrology or transplantation and to mitigate the shortage of specialists in
the field of urology and transplantation:
(5) to undertake. training of
nursing and Para‑medical staff including technicians both graduates and
post‑graduates in the field of urology and transplantation;
(6) to carry out and promote research, surveys,
experiments and demonstrations in urological diseases for prevention and
control of such diseases;
(7) to publish research papers,
studies and such other works as are completed at the Institute or are prepared
in collaboration with any other similar institute or agency, local or foreign
or which are otherwise of substantial value to the Institute;
(8) to organize seminars and
conferences to promote cooperation with national and international agencies in
activities falling within the purview of the Institute;
(9) to undertake all such activities or do such other
acts and things as may help to further the objects of the Institute.

5. Administration of the affairs of the Institute.‑‑The general
direction and administration of the Institute and its affairs shall vest in a
Board to be called the Board of Governors which may exercise all powers and do
all acts and things which ri1ay be exercised or done by the Institute.

(2) The Board may associate such other experts as it

(3) A member, other than ex officio member, may

(4) Unless a member ceases to hold office or removed

(5) When a person is appointed to be a member by
virtue of his holding an office, he shall cease to be such member when he

sections.shortTitle: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Act 1991
sections.description:
Meetings of the board

ACT II OF 1991
ACT II OF 1991
SINDH INSTITUTE OF UROLOGY AND
TRANSPLANTATION ACT, 1991
9. Meetings of the Board.‑‑(1) The Board
shall meet at least twice in a year with a gap of at least three months on the
dates to be fixed by the Director in consultation with the Chairman:
Provided that the Chairman may convene a meeting at
any time.
(2) The Chairman shall preside over the meeting.
(3) In the absence of the Chairman, the meeting may
be presided over by the Vice‑Chairman and in the absence of both, by the
member to be appointed by the members present.
(4) The quorum for a meeting
shall be one‑third of the total number of members, a fraction being
counted as one, but no‑quorum shall be necessary for the meeting held in
lieu of the meeting which was adjourned for want of quorum.
(5) The Chairman shall have and exercise a casting
vote in the case of a tie.
(6)' The Secretary of the Board shall record the
minutes of meeting which shall be submitted by him at the next meeting for
confirmation.

sections.shortTitle: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Act 1991
sections.description:
Director of the institute

ACT II OF 1991
ACT II OF 1991
SINDH INSTITUTE OF UROLOGY AND
TRANSPLANTATION ACT, 1991
10. Director of the Institute.‑‑The
Director to be appointed by the Board on the prescribed terms and conditions
shall possess prescribed qualifications from a University established by law in
Pakistan or a University of .International repute and shall have experience of
teaching courses relating to urology and transplantation in a recognized
University for at least ten years:
Provided that the person holding office of the
Professor of the Urology and Transplantation Department of the Dow Medical
College immediately before the commencement of the Sindh Institute of Urology
and Transplantation Ordinance, 1990 (Sindh Ordinance No. III of 1990) shall be
the first Director of the Institute.

sections.shortTitle: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Act 1991
sections.description:
Powers of the directors

ACT II OF 1991
ACT II OF 1991
SINDH INSTITUTE OF UROLOGY AND
TRANSPLANTATION ACT, 1991
11. Powers of the Director.‑‑(l) The
Director shall be the academic and executive head of the Institute and shall
administer the affairs of the Institute to accordance with the provisions of
this Act and regulations and shall have the following powers and functions:‑‑
(i) to keep in custody the records and seal of the
Institute;
(ii) to authorise payments of monthly salaries and
allowances to the employees of or the persons working in the Institute;
(iii) to prepare budget estimates and supplementary
budget estimates and place the same before the Board for approval;
(iv) to pass payment, of bills under any heads of the
budget duly approved and authorised;
(v) to act as Secretary of the Board and issue
notices of meetings of the Board and its committees in consultation with the
Chairman and to prepare and maintain minutes and record and proceedings of the
meetings;
(vi) to take steps for the
implementation of decisions of the Board;
(vii) to prepare and present
the annual budget;
(viii) to carry on all the
correspondence of the Institute;
(ix) to execute deeds and
documents on behalf of the Board; and
(x) to perform any other duties which may be assigned
to him by the Board.
(2) The Director shall be the ex officio member of a
committee or sub‑committee set up by the Board.
(3) The Director shall not except with the previous
approval of the Board in each case or unless already approved in the budget
duly itemised, allow expenditure on items of civil works, or capital
expenditure on equipment or automobiles.
(4) The Director may delegate such of his powers to
any other officer or committee of the Institute as he deems fit.

sections.shortTitle: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Act 1991
sections.description:
Academic council

ACT II OF 1991
ACT II OF 1991

TRANSPLANTATION ACT, 1991
12. Academic Council.‑‑(1) The Institute
shall have an Academic Council which shall perform such functions as may be
assigned to it by the Board under this Act or regulations.
(2) The Academic Council shall consist of the
following:‑‑
.(i) Director. Chairman.
(ii) Principal of the Dow
Medical College. Member.
(iii) All Professors and
Associate Professors
of the Institute. Members.
(3) The Academic Council may associate such other
experts as it may consider necessary.
(4) The meetings of the Council shall be held as
frequently as possible, but not less than four times a year.
(5) The quorum of a meeting shall be one‑half
of the total number of the members of the Academic Council, a fraction being
counted as one.

sections.shortTitle: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Act 1991
sections.description:
Terms and conditions of service  etc of Government servants working in the institute

ACT II OF 1991
ACT II OF 1991
SINDH INSTITUTE OF UROLOGY AND
TRANSPLANTATION ACT, 1991
13. Terms and conditions of service etc., of Government servants working in the
Institute.‑‑(1) All persons in the service of Government
serving in the Urology Department of the Dow Medical College in any capacity
immediately before the commencement of the Sindh Institute of Urology and
Transplantation Ordinance, 1990 (Sindh Ordinance No.III of 1990) shall stand
transferred for service under the Institute:
Provided that such persons shall‑‑
(i) continue to be civil servants;
(ii) be entitled to receive from the Institute for
the period of their service under the Institute, pay and allowances which shall
not be less than those to which they were entitled immediately before their transfer
to the Institute;
(iii) be governed by such regulations as the
Institute may, with the approval of Government, make; provided that such
regulations shall not be less favourable than the rules applicable to them
immediately before their transfer to the Institute.
(2) The Institute shall, in respect of the persons
whose services have been transferred to it under subsection (1)‑‑
(i) exercise all such administrative and financial
powers as were exercisable by Government or any authority subordinate to that
Government; and
(ii) initiate disciplinary proceedings against any
such person and refer the case of such person to Government for further action.
(3) The persons whose services have been transferred
to the Institute under subsection (1) shall be entitled to receive from
Government for the whole of their service, including the service under the
Institute, pension and the amount of commutation of pension in accordance with
the rules applicable to them:
Provided that the Institute shall pay to Government
in respect of each such person a sum equal to the sum which bears the same
proportion to the total sum paid to such person as the total period of service
of such person bears to the period of service rendered by him in the Institute.
(4) The pension and the amount of commutation of
pension shall be sanctioned by such officer of the Institute as Government may
authorise in this behalf:
Provided that, if such pension is required to be
reduced, such officer shall, before sanctioning such pension, obtain formal
orders of Government.
(5) The General Provident Fund accumulations of the
persons whose services have been transferred to the Institute under subsection
(1) shall remain with Government, and they shall continue to contribute
'towards their Provident Fund account:
Provided that temporary advances from such Fund may
be sanctioned by the Institute in accordance with the rules applicable to them.

14. Appointments
and terms and conditions of Officers and staff of the Institute.‑‑(l)
The Institute may for efficient performance of its functions appoint such
officers and staff possessing such professional, technical or ministerial
qualifications and experience in such manner and on such terms and conditions
as may be prescribed.
(2) The officers and staff shall be liable to such
disciplinary actions and in such manner as may be prescribed.

sections.shortTitle: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Act 1991
sections.description:
Fund

ACT II OF 1991
ACT II OF 1991
SINDH INSTITUTE OF UROLOGY AND
TRANSPLANTATION ACT, 1991
15. Fund.‑‑(1) There shall be a separate
fund of the Institute known as the Sindh Institute of Urology and
Transplantation Fund.
(2) The Fund shall consist of‑‑
(a) grants and subsidy received from the Federal and
Provincial Governments;
(b) donations and endowments;
(c) income from investments and
deposits;
(d) loans raised or aid
obtained by the Institute;
(e) fees, royalties on publications of the Institute
and other charges for services rendered by the Institute;
(f) grants made by any Local
Authority; and
(g) all moneys received from any donor agency of
Pakistan or foreign origin.

21. Bar of jurisdiction.‑‑No Court shall
have jurisdiction to entertain any proceedings, grant any injunction or make
any order in relation to anything done or purported to have been done or
intended to be done in. good faith under this Ordinance.

suit or legal proceedings shall lie against Government, the Board or any person

been done in good faith purported to have been under this Act.
